label: copy phase: input l with 2 as the next output (the l->2 bigram being recalled)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost only (97% of mass) when the fed-back input is l. It is strongest when the token being output right after that l is 2, so the original contained the bigram l 2: every top example is ...l 2 being recalled, and out_tok=2 carries 73% of mass. It needs recall_idx >= 3 (it is silent at recall 0-1 and weak at 2). The predicate in=l & out=2 & recall>=3 has about 0.88 precision but only about half the recall. The rest is weaker firing on input l when the output is something else, mostly l (l l) or 3, plus a small amount (3%) on input 2. Bare copy-phase input l has very low precision (0.04), so the output token matters. Never fires in the original or delimiter phases, or when in_tok is the first occurrence of that token.
